clue.text: Timid cow that's seen at the front of the field?

definitions.text: that's seen at the front of the field?

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly or timid
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A shy cow out in a meadow, the one that stands at the front of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The field is the pack of riders in a cycle race, not a meadow. The yellow jersey is worn by the overall leader of the Tour de France.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Tour de France the race leader wears this shirt, so it is out in front of the pack of cyclists.

clue.text: In auditorium, second person will record cake

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: the second person is you, will record is 'll log, giving you'll log

explanation.surface: In a concert hall, a second person is going to note down details of a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You'll log' (you will record) is said the same as 'Yule log'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yule log is a chocolate sponge roll shaped like a log, eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: European's muscle getting unit inside truck

parts.note: lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle

indicators.note: getting here means going, with inside: the unit goes into the vehicle
inside means the unit is placed within the truck's letters

parts.note: a van is a small truck
I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit

explanation.surface: A European's brawn being put to work loading a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latvian is a person from Latvia, a country in Europe's Baltic region.

clue.text: Quiz man Richard introduces Mike, friend and moderator

indicators.note: the quiz host's name takes in the other pieces, as if introducing them onto his show

parts.note: Richard Osman is a British TV quiz presenter (Pointless, House of Games)
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
bud is slang for a friend

explanation.surface: A TV quiz host brings on a contestant called Mike, a pal, and an adjudicator.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Osman is a British TV quiz show host (Pointless); 'introduces' slips the other pieces in just after his surname's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official who looks into complaints and settles them, a kind of moderator between parties.

clue.text: Devout patriot, on disc, telling gags? Not OK

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
Not tells us those two letters are to be left out of the word before

parts.note: telling gags means joking
O is a disc, by its round shape

explanation.surface: A fervent nationalist goes on the radio cracking jokes that aren't acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not OK' is an instruction, not a comment on the jokes: strike those two letters out. 'disc' is O by its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A jingo is a loud, warlike nationalist, an extreme or devout kind of patriot.

clue.text: Cowboy builder's latest alteration extremely dear, according to Rene

indicators.note: the latest letter of the word is its final one
the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: cher is French for dear; Rene stands for any French speaker

explanation.surface: A dodgy cowboy builder's newest alteration is very pricey, so says a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowboy builder' reads as one phrase for a rogue tradesman, but only 'Cowboy' is the definition. R is the last of 'builder's', AN the ends of 'alteration'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a cattle ranch, much as a cowboy herds cattle on one.

clue.text: Character in Marathon that follows delta

definitions.text: Character in Marathon that follows delta

parts.words: Character in Marathon that follows delta
parts.note: Marathon is in Greece, so the character is a Greek letter, and the one after delta in that alphabet is the fifth

explanation.surface: A runner in a marathon who trails behind someone from a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter, not a person; Marathon points to Greek, and delta is the fourth Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, coming straight after delta.

clue.text: Open program by fish expert

parts.note: an app is a computer program
the roach is a freshwater fish
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A fishing app is open to all, written by an angler who knows his stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone approachable is friendly and easy to talk to, which is what open means of a person.

clue.text: Opener, awfully tall, in The Cricketers Arms?

indicators.note: one piece in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: The Cricketers Arms is a typical name for a pub; the question mark shows it is an example

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A very tall batsman opens the innings, drinking at the local cricket pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a cricket batsman, but it is a thing that opens a can. 'awfully' scrambles 'tall' inside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pull-tab is the ring or strip you tug on a can to get it open, so it is an opener.

clue.text: One's clean load put in corner, half aired

indicators.note: one piece put in another is placed inside it
only half the word is aired, that is shown; here its back half

parts.note: onus means a burden or load

explanation.surface: Someone tidy shoves a load of washing in the corner, half dried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aired' looks like laundry talk but means shown: only half of 'corner' appears. 'clean' here means drug-free.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-user takes no drugs, which is what being clean means in drug slang.

clue.text: Maybe study leading novel of the 1950s

parts.note: a study is one example of a room
leading means being at the top

explanation.surface: Perhaps a study of a famous 1950s novel is the most influential one.
explanation.walkthrough: Room at the Top (1957) is John Braine's novel about an ambitious young man in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Room at the Top is John Braine's 1957 novel, later filmed, so it is a novel from that decade.

clue.text: Participated in demo song with artist and student

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
L is a learner, as on L-plates
a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: At a protest, a singer, a painter and a college kid all join in.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to gather at a mass protest meeting, so rallied means took part in a demo.

clue.text: Play the empty local when in bands

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the two rings

parts.note: two Os look like two rings or bands

indicators.note: an empty word loses its insides, keeping just the outside letters

explanation.surface: A play put on in the deserted pub when the bands are on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Shakespeare tragedy about the Moor of Venice and the scheming Iago.

clue.text: Element of technical language Jack ignored

indicators.note: a letter ignored is left out of the word

parts.note: jargon is the specialist language of a trade
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: Part of the specialist lingo that someone called Jack paid no heed to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of' reads as 'part of', but Element is the definition, a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, one of the chemical elements, number 18.

clue.text: Joggers Mike and American circling Italian city in recession

indicators.note: the outer pieces go round the city, enclosing it

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: recession is going back, so the city is read backwards

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Runners named Mike and an American jog round Rome as the economy shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joggers' looks like runners; it means things that jog the memory. 'in recession' reads the city backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are notes that jog the memory, so joggers in that sense.

clue.text: Problem lifting lino's bothered one supremo in the past

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem

indicators.note: something bothered is stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to pick up linoleum is troubled, a one-time boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns SUM into MUS; 'bothered' makes SOLIN from LINOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was Italy's Fascist dictator, called Il Duce, a supreme leader of the past.

clue.text: Part of newspaper's front page wrinkles?

definitions.meaning: the large titles printed on a newspaper's front page
lines on the head, that is creases on the forehead; the question mark marks the wordplay sense

explanation.surface: Is the front of the paper creased?
explanation.definitionFit: Headlines are big printed titles; read as head lines, they are creases on the brow.

clue.text: Fan heard reworking by Queen

indicators.note: reworking means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A fan heard a remixed track by the band Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent or supporter, such as a fan of a cause, is someone who sticks to it.

clue.text: Business graduate participates in final lecture

indicators.note: one piece participates in another by joining it, going inside

parts.note: last means final
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A business graduate attends the end-of-term lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to scold harshly, as in giving someone a stern lecture, the verb sense.

clue.text: English stream divided on Beckett ultimately

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it
ultimately points to the word's final letter

parts.note: rent means torn apart, divided

explanation.surface: An English river splits opinion, on the subject of Samuel Beckett.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands, a stream in the broad sense.

clue.text: Fabulous plant pruned by constant champion

indicators.note: a pruned word is cut back, losing its last letter

parts.note: the triffid is the fictional man-eating plant of John Wyndham's novel
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A marvellous plant is cut back by a steady prize-winning gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like the definition, but it describes the fictional plant. Triffic and champion are both British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion is old British slang for excellent, and triffic is a jokey form of terrific with the same meaning.

clue.text: Old record company detailed immature female expatriate

parts.note: EMI is the historic British record label

indicators.note: a word detailed loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: green means immature or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A former record label gave the details of a young woman living abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigree is the feminine form of emigre, a person who has left their country to live elsewhere.

clue.text: Snake around border with India, finding ancient kingdom

indicators.note: the snake goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a boa is a large snake
a hem is the edge or border of cloth
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A snake found on the frontier with India, in an old realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia was a kingdom in central Europe, now the western part of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Improvised band she once observed regularly

indicators.note: only every other letter is observed, the regular ones

explanation.surface: A group she used to watch often played off the cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc means arranged for the moment without planning, much the same as improvised.

clue.text: During Noel essentially detectives on team become rusty

indicators.note: the pieces come during the other, inside it
the essence of the word is its core, the middle letters
in an across clue, a piece on another follows it

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: At Christmas, police officers in the side lose their sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives OE from 'Noel'. 'Noel' looks like a name, not Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: To oxidise is to combine with oxygen, and iron rusts by doing exactly that.

clue.text: Harry's personal audio system complements party

parts.note: jokingly, the ear is everyone's own built-in audio system
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: Harry's headphones go perfectly with the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry's' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb harry, with the 's standing for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Earbash is Australian slang for talking at someone at length, a way to harass or pester them.

clue.text: Wise perhaps to interrupt dope creating flames

indicators.note: a piece that interrupts another breaks into it, going inside

parts.note: dope is slang for information, info
Ern was Eric Morecambe's name for his partner Ernie Wise, of the British comedy duo Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A wise person cuts in on someone high, causing a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like an adjective; it is Ernie Wise of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise, known as Ern.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a huge blazing fire, a mass of flames.

clue.text: Freezing underground line, a line on some maps

parts.note: arctic means freezing cold
the Circle line is on the London Underground

explanation.surface: A chilly Tube line, which shows up on some maps.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic Circle is the line of latitude at about 66 degrees north, drawn on many maps.
